datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) relative humidity sensor (RHS) measurements
datasets.instrument_sensor: Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) relative humidity sensor (RHS)
datasets.measurement_observable: Air relative humidity with respect to ice (RHi_a) at 1.6 m height and air temperature (Ta) entering the RHS; derived/inferred ground relative humidity (RHi_g) and relative humidity with respect to liquid (RHl_g); inferred water vapor pressure (PH2O)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: First 1648 sols of MSL mission operations at Gale crater (includes specific mention of sols 1232 and 1311; Ls 99° and Ls 137°)
datasets.location_coverage: Gale crater, Mars; landing site/floor of Gale crater at 4.7°S, 137°E; measurements at 1.6 m height on rover mast along Curiosity’s traverse
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: Nominal strategy: 5 min of measurements at 1 Hz every Mars hour, with interspersed full-hour sample periods at 1 Hz; analysis used only the first 4 s after RHS turn-on after ~5 min of inactivity; results typically produced 24 hourly values per sol under nominal strategy; high-resolution interval mode used on selected 1–2 hr observation blocks
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Updated calibrations to REMS data (latest calibration noted as June 2015); analysis restricted to highest-confidence measurements and applied sensor-heating filter (first 4 s)
datasets.pds_identifiers: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), Planetary Atmospheres Node (REMS data stated as publicly available there)
datasets.how_used: Primary observational input for assessing whether near-surface humidity–temperature conditions permit deliquescence of Ca(ClO4)2: used RHi_a and Ta (filtered to minimize sensor self-heating) to compute/infer PH2O and convert/infer ground relative humidity in both RHi and RHl phase space for comparison with calcium perchlorate phase diagrams; also used to construct nighttime vapor-pressure curves and derive enthalpy changes via Clausius–Clapeyron analysis.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) ground temperature sensor (GTS) measurements
datasets.instrument_sensor: Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) ground temperature sensor (GTS)
datasets.measurement_observable: Ground-emitted infrared intensity used to derive surface brightness/ground temperature (Tg)
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ infrared ground-temperature time-series measurements
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: First 1648 sols of MSL mission operations at Gale crater
datasets.location_coverage: Gale crater, Mars; GTS thermopiles pointed 26° downward from rover deck plane; field of view 60° horizontally and 40° vertically, covering a ground area of about 100 m² depending on surface/sensor angle
datasets.spatial_resolution: Ground footprint about 100 m² (depends on surface/sensor angle)
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: Used measurements averaged over 5-min intervals centered at simultaneous highest-confidence RHS measurements; required at least 60 GTS measurements per 5-min interval to reduce noise (to produce high-quality hourly Tg values simultaneous to RHS)
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Analysis used only GTS measurements with highest confidence (ASIC power supply in range, highest recalibration quality, and no shadows in GTS field of view) and 5-min averaging/quality filtering
datasets.pds_identifiers: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), Planetary Atmospheres Node (REMS data stated as publicly available there)
datasets.how_used: Used to derive high-quality hourly ground temperature (Tg) simultaneous with RHS humidity observations; Tg was used to infer ground relative humidity and to compare (Tg, RH) conditions against calcium perchlorate deliquescence/efflorescence phase boundaries; Tg also used (with inferred PH2O) to build vapor-pressure curves and derive nighttime enthalpy changes, and to validate/model surface boundary conditions in subsurface simulations.
